correctness.rationale: For arbitrary prime powers and m,n>=2, derive the known rank-one Fourier sum by explicit nonzero-u,v counting, independently of citations. Pairwise selected frequency differences have rank 0, 1, or 2 and yield exactly the claimed G matrix. Its label-sum-zero, row, column, and interaction spaces have the stated dimensions and eigenvalues, while the zero-frequency plus uniform-label two-dimensional block has exactly roots lambda_+/- and explicitly computed eigenvectors. Positivity of this last block follows from nonconstant rank-one support product, with determinant equal to its variance divided by T. All multiplicities total 1+mn(q-1), so no missing spectrum. Parseval/Rayleigh prove the sharp energy bound, and trace/determinant expansion proves the fixed-q square asymptotic. checker.py independently passed complete Gram and multiplicity-sensitive eigenvalue comparisons for twelve cases, including GF(4); finite tests do not prove the unrestricted formulas. No external independent validation is asserted.

value.rationale: The Segre rank-one shell is a canonical finite-field matrix variety and the complete first-coordinate Fourier band is the natural degree-one character model. The theorem supplies all singular values and equality spaces, proves injectivity for every field, and quantifies its unavoidable condition degradation with the nontrivial cubic squared-condition law in square dimension. Neither a renamed full rank-scheme Fourier coefficient nor an arbitrary small numerical slice; the selected-band spectral stability problem has a motivated exact answer, with explicit scope limitations.
